text:
Marco (Acme): hey team — hitting a weird streaming issue on our Dedicated cluster (ded-12, eu-west-1). When our client reconnects after a short network blip it often resumes but then stalls (no more events) for 10–30s, then jumps back with a bunch of tokens. Looks like partial SSE payloads get swallowed or merged by our corp proxy. Using VPC with MTU=1400 on the peered link.

Aisha (Support): thanks Marco — can you paste a minimal repro curl or client snippet and a request id / trace id from one of the failed sessions? also is the client behind a corporate proxy or inline appliance?

Marco (Acme): here's a quick curl from the client side that shows it:

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/session?session_id=abc123" \
  -v
```

Output truncates mid-event:
```
event: message
data: {"tokens": "This is a partial toke"
```
then nothing until reconnect. Request id header on the response: X-Request-Id: r-0a7d3b2c.

Elliot (Customer Eng): adding that we see duplicate billing events when the client reconnects (the server emits tokens before the resume token is acknowledged), so the customer sometimes gets double-charged for the same partial output.

Aisha (Support): ugh — duplication + stall is high severity. @Leo can you take a look for networking/proxy shenanigans?

Leo (SRE): jumping in. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) the corporate proxy is aggregating TCP application writes into different TCP segments (MTU/PMTU/clamping or proxy buffering), then on resume the client receives a corrupted chunk boundary so the SSE parser blocks until next newline. 2) kernel offload (GRO/LRO) or Nagle + buffering on the proxy causing delayed flushes. Both can produce the stall + burst behavior.

Priya (Infra): on Dedicated nodes we recently enabled tcp_mtu_probing=0 for perf tests. If the peering path has an MTU mismatch (1400 vs 1500 somewhere) we can get blackhole fragmentation that shows as partial TCP frames at the app layer. Can you confirm the corp proxy type/version? Squid? F5? BlueCorp Edge?

Marco (Acme): It's a BlueCorp proxy appliance (BlueEdge v2.3) doing TLS termination and HTTP/1.1 reverse-proxying with proxy buffering on by default. They say they can't change firmware quickly.

Aisha (Support): ok actionable repro steps for customer + our infra:
1) Customer: run curl with --no-buffer/-N and save a pcap of the session so we can see where chunk boundaries land. Example:
```
sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.example and port 443 -s 0 -w acme_stream.pcap
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/session?session_id=abc123" -o /dev/null
```
2) Customer: also run a raw repro directly to the node ip (skip proxy) if possible to confirm proxy is the culprit:
```
curl -N --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.2.3.45 "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/session?..."
```
3) Our side: enable a temporary debug trace on the ingress for request id r-0a7d3b2c and capture server-side tcpdump for the same interval.

Leo (SRE): adding a quick node repro you can run to simulate flaky proxy chunking — streams small writes with flush: 

```
// node repro (client-like)
const https = require('https');
const opts = { hostname: 'api.redwood.example', path: '/v1/streams/session?session_id=test', headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' } };
https.get(opts, (res) => {
  res.on('data', (chunk) => { process.stdout.write(chunk); });
});

// on the server side, if the proxy merges writes into a single segment the client parser may block
```

Priya (Infra): infra checks to run on our dedicated nodes:
- Check net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing (set to 1 to enable PMTU probing): `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`
- Disable GRO/LRO on the interface for the test: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off` (only for debugging)
- Verify kernel TCP settings around timestamps and delayed_ack.

Aisha (Support): thanks — @Marco can you request an emergency config tweak from BlueCorp to temporarily disable proxy buffering for the streaming path (or add `proxy_buffering off`/`Transfer-Encoding: chunked` passthrough). If they can't, we have two mitigations: 1) server-side produce an explicit keepalive comment line every 1–2s to force flush (`: keepalive\n\n`), 2) enable a short resume grace window on the client to dedupe tokens for 2s before billing.

Marco (Acme): BlueCorp will only accept a config change if we provide the exact nginx-like snippet. can you provide one?

Aisha (Support): sample nginx proxy config to preserve SSE chunk boundaries (ask BlueCorp to add to their reverse-proxy location):

```
location /v1/streams/ {
  proxy_pass https://origin-uw1;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_set_header Host $host;
}
```

Aisha (Support): also ask them to disable any response body buffering or gzip for that path.

Leo (SRE): additional low-level mitigation we can try if proxy changes aren't possible:
- Turn on more frequent SSE keepalives (`:ka\n\n`) from the runtime to keep the parser moving.
- Set resume tokens to be confirmed server-side before continuing to emit downstream tokens (makes resume slightly higher-latency but avoids dupes).

Priya (Infra): long-term we should detect when a customer path has MTU < 1500 and enable MSS clamping on the egress (iptables mangle rule) for that VPC peering. Example command to clamp MSS on the border router: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`. Also consider enabling `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on the Dedicated node set.

Marco (Acme): we'll try the curl + pcap and ask BlueCorp to add the proxy snippet for the streaming path. If they refuse, we'll ask you to enable the keepalive patch on ded-12.

Aisha (Support): action items: 
- Marco: upload acme_stream.pcap and the curl output, and confirm if direct-to-node works.
- Leo: enable server-side tcpdump for request id r-0a7d3b2c window and check for partial packet boundaries.
- Priya: prepare an infra patch to flip tcp_mtu_probing=1 and turn off GRO for debugging on ded-12.
- Product: consider adding a runtime flag to make resume token acknowledgement mandatory before continuing token emission (will open a short RFC).

deploy-bot: [canary-rollback] ded-runtime/ded-12 -> rolled back to v2026.03.11 (reason: temporary instrumentation for streaming diagnostics).

Leo (SRE): timeline — we'll have initial tcpdump + pcap correlation in ~4h, infra change to test in 24h. If customer provides pcap earlier we can speed this up.

Marco (Acme): thanks all — will upload pcap and keep you posted. appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
